summary: Per-connection vs API-key quota drift when mixing long-lived WebSocket sessions and short bulk ingestion
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurrent 429s and apparent quota drift when they run a steady set of long-lived websocket chat sessions in parallel with periodic bulk embedding uploads. The customer expects per-API-key accounting to remain stable regardless of connection pattern, but observed token/quota counters moving unexpectedly during bulk runs.

Impact:
- Several end-user chat sessions receiving transient 429s during nightly embedding backfills.
- Bulk ingestion jobs intermittently fail and require retries, increasing cost and delaying data availability.
- Customer concerned about accuracy of quota metering for billing reconciliation.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-east-1, tenant: dataripple-prod (dedicated).
- WebSocket clients maintain long-lived streaming connections (avg 45-90 minutes).
- Bulk ingestion uses parallel workers starting 120 concurrent short-lived HTTP sessions to the embeddings endpoint.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start 200 long-lived websocket streams using api key X (each stream sends ~5 tokens/s).
2) Kick off a bulk embedding job: 120 parallel short HTTP POSTs each sending batches of 512 texts.
3) Observe quota headers and success rates for ~10 minutes.
4) Note 429 spikes reported by websocket clients and bulk workers intermittently.

Expected behaviour:
- Token/quota accounting remains consistent at the api-key / tenant level and 429s are surfaced only when the agreed quota is exhausted. Long-lived streams should not cause per-connection double-counting when parallel short sessions open/close.

Observed behaviour:
- Customer sees quota depletion messages attributed to short HTTP sessions while websocket sessions also report 429s. Header X-RateLimit-Remaining sometimes shows large drops synchronized with bulk job start. After bulk job completes, counts stabilize but some websocket sessions remain rate-limited for a short window.

Initial hypothesis:
- Possible double-counting when HTTP/2 or multiplexed connections share underlying sockets (connection-level counters vs token-level counters).
- Quota service may be aggregating per-connection tokens into per-key windows with a short reconciliation delay, causing transient over-consumption to be reflected across active connections.
- Dedicated pool autoscaler or routing handoff at the proxy layer could increment ephemeral counters during worker churn.
logs:
Customer provided sample headers and timestamps:
- 2026-02-26T23:01:12Z websocket stream id ws-102: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 3482, status 200
- 2026-02-26T23:05:03Z bulk-worker-17 POST /v1/embeddings: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 289, status 429
- 2026-02-26T23:05:04Z websocket stream id ws-120: status 429, retry-after: 3
Logs show bulk workers making bursts of large payloads; gateway logs show short-lived upstream connections closed and reopened during the window. Gateway trace: trace_id=c1a4b2, route=embeddings, proxied_to=embed-node-7
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced locally in staging by running 50 long websockets + 30 parallel embedding POSTs; observed a small window where quota headers were decremented faster than expected.
- Captured gateway traces showing per-connection token accounting emitted on connect and on close; a race condition in the aggregator task increments both per-connection and per-request counters for the same tokens when connections tear down concurrently.
- Quota service processes reports from streaming-proxy every 10s; bulk ingestion path reports per-request immediately. During high churn, the aggregator double-applies a 'recently-closed' delta.
- No evidence of tenant-level bug in billing pipeline; this appears to be transient accounting in the in-memory quota cache in the quota-service shim.
- Related PR touching aggregator timing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3442 (open, awaiting review).
comments: 2026-02-28 Maya Chen: Customer opened ticket — they provided header dumps and a short gateway pcap. Expecting guidance and (if necessary) hotfix prioritisation.
2026-03-01 Diego Ramos: Assigned for triage. Reproduced a similar pattern in staging; collecting traces and heap profiles. Marking as P2 pending customer impact confirmation.

2026-03-02 SRE (Arjun Patel): Heapshot shows quota-aggregator backlog spikes during bulk job start. Suggest applying a short-term rate-smoothing on the gateway to prevent burstbackfill from causing immediate per-key exhaustion.

2026-03-03 Solutions Eng (Lina Morales): Customer requests a mitigation that doesn't require code changes. Recommended two actions: 1) run bulk ingestion from a separate API key with its own quota bucket; 2) stage bulk jobs to ramp-up concurrency over 5 minutes instead of instant fanout. Customer will try separate key first.

2026-03-05 Diego Ramos: Engineering will propose a patch to the aggregator to debounce 'connection closed' deltas for 15s and to ensure idempotent application of token counts. Opening internal PR and linking to this ticket. Temporary workaround documented below.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: recommend customer create a dedicated API key for bulk ingestion (separate quota bucket) and stagger worker fanout using exponential ramp (5m). Engineering change: patch to quota-aggregator to debounce closed-connection deltas and add idempotency keys for per-connection reports (PR opened). Follow-up: monitor for 72h after deploy and confirm with customer that websocket 429s no longer correlate with bulk job start.
next_steps:
- Engineering to scope and land aggregator debounce patch (ETA 2026-03-10).
- Customer to test separate API key for bulk jobs and report results by 2026-03-06.
- SRE to add a Grafana panel showing short-window delta between per-connection and per-key counters to detect regressions.
- If workaround insufficient, schedule hotfix rollout to dedicated pool.
